sealedSource: Structurally modelled on shelf-sea fishery collapses where stable catches masked depletion under increasing effort.
archetype: Fragile commons with hysteresis — the case where feedback-sensitive regulation fails and a precautionary floor is required.
historicallySupportedMechanisms: Stable landings under rising effort/gear efficiency concealed depletion of the underlying stock.
A slow review cadence meant feedback arrived after the recruitment threshold could be crossed.
Protecting part of the fleet in the short term increased the probability of losing the entire fishery later.
materialisedConsequences: The entire fleet lost its livelihood, not half of it
Stock did not recover after closure; the ecosystem shifted to a different state
Communities lost the industry permanently rather than temporarily
irreversibleThreshold: Stock recruitment threshold — below it the population did not recover even with fishing stopped entirely.
absentStakeholder: Future fishers and the communities' own next generation; the stock itself as a party rather than a resource.
narratorContribution: The narrator adopted the fleet's inference from stable landings while holding the advisers' explanation of why that inference fails — and chose the reading that deferred the cost.
horizonMismatch: Decision horizon one season; ecological recovery horizon decades or never; the narrator recorded the recovery horizon correctly and did not act on it.

availableActionsAtDecisionPoint.action: Adopt the scientific advisers' recommended 40% catch reduction rather than the proposed 10% cut.

plausibleUnrealisedRisks: A 40% quota cut could force roughly half of small boats out of business within a season.
irrelevantDistractors: Scientific advice being materially too alarmist
nonTargetHistoricalEvents: Fuel-price increases occurred but were not decisive.
Processing-plant closure was a consequence rather than the causal mechanism.
